answer_text:
Let

\[
A=\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^4}}, 
\qquad 
B=\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}.
\]

We want \(A/B\).

First evaluate \(A\). Put \(u=t^4\), so \(dt=\frac14 u^{-3/4}\,du\). Then

\[
A=\frac14\int_0^1 u^{-3/4}(1-u)^{-1/2}\,du
=\frac14 B\!\left(\frac14,\frac12\right).
\]

Next evaluate \(B\). Consider

\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}.
\]

By substituting \(t=1/u\) on \([1,\infty)\), we get

\[
\int_1^\infty \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}
=\int_0^1 \frac{du}{\sqrt{1+u^4}}=B.
\]

Therefore

\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}=2B.
\]

Now substitute \(u=t^4\):

\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}
=\frac14\int_0^\infty u^{-3/4}(1+u)^{-1/2}\,du.
\]

Using the Euler beta integral

\[
\int_0^\infty u^{a-1}(1+u)^{-a-b}\,du=B(a,b),
\]

with \(a=\frac14\) and \(a+b=\frac12\), so \(b=\frac14\), we obtain

\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^4}}
=\frac14 B\!\left(\frac14,\frac14\right).
\]

Thus

\[
B=\frac18 B\!\left(\frac14,\frac14\right).
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{A}{B}
=
\frac{\frac14 B\left(\frac14,\frac12\right)}
{\frac18 B\left(\frac14,\frac14\right)}
=
2\frac{B\left(\frac14,\frac12\right)}
{B\left(\frac14,\frac14\right)}.
\]

Using \(B(p,q)=\frac{\Gamma(p)\Gamma(q)}{\Gamma(p+q)}\),

\[
\frac{A}{B}
=
2\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac14\right)\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)/\Gamma\left(\frac34\right)}
{\Gamma\left(\frac14\right)^2/\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)}
=
\frac{2\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)^2}{\Gamma\left(\frac14\right)\Gamma\left(\frac34\right)}.
\]

Since \(\Gamma\left(\frac12\right)=\sqrt\pi\) and by the reflection formula

\[
\Gamma\left(\frac14\right)\Gamma\left(\frac34\right)
=
\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi/4)}
=
\pi\sqrt2,
\]

we get

\[
\frac{A}{B}
=
\frac{2\pi}{\pi\sqrt2}
=
\sqrt2.
\]

\[
\boxed{\sqrt2}
\]
